Month in brief

Edge for Business gains cross-tenant MAM as Intune’s compliance guidance expands

April’s clearest service-level change is a Message Center major update: Edge for Business now supports opt-in cross-tenant Intune MAM policies for devices managed by different tenants, including app protection, OneDrive download redirection, and leak controls. The other selected items are primarily new Learn guidance or support documentation—not proof that a new feature launched. The third-party compliance list is explicitly labeled generally available, while the EPM, WSL, and Enterprise App Catalog entries provide rollout procedures and operational clarification.

  • Intune · App management
    Edge for Business adds opt-in cross-tenant Intune MAM

    The Message Center major update says Edge for Business can apply Intune MAM policies on devices managed by a different tenant. The opt-in feature enforces app protection, redirects downloads to OneDrive, and activates leak controls. This is a product behavior update, not a documentation-only addition.

  • Intune · Device security
    Third-party compliance partner support is documented as generally available

    The new Intune overview labels its supported partner list as generally available, including Jamf Pro, Kandji, Ivanti Neurons for MDM, and Omnissa Workspace ONE UEM. It says partner-collected state is added to Microsoft Entra ID and that the partner becomes the MDM authority for devices assigned through an Entra user group. The documented sequence is to configure Intune and groups, configure the partner to send data, and then enroll devices.

  • Endpoint Privilege Management · Device security
    EPM guidance prescribes audit-first migration from administrator to standard user

    The new Endpoint Privilege Management guide sets an audit-first path. Its example policy uses Endpoint Privilege Management: Enabled; Default elevation response: Not Configured; Send elevation data for reporting: Yes; and Reporting scope: Diagnostic data and all endpoint elevations. It says reporting data can take 24 hours to return and may warrant observation over many weeks. This is rollout guidance, not a new EPM availability announcement.

  • Intune · Device security
    WSL compliance guidance names plugin, management-extension, and cleanup prerequisites

    The new Intune WSL procedure requires the Intune WSL plugin and the Intune management extension. The extension can be installed when a PowerShell script or proactive remediation, Win32 or Microsoft Store app, or custom compliance policy is assigned. Before starting, administrators must unassign and remove existing custom compliance policies for WSL. The page documents how WSL results contribute to the host device’s compliance state; it does not by itself prove a new feature launch.

  • Enterprise App Management · App management
    Enterprise App Catalog guidance sets validated defaults and update expectations

    The new Enterprise App Management procedure says Microsoft configures and confirms default installation, requirements, and detection settings for catalog apps, and warns that changing install or uninstall commands can introduce unexpected or harmful commands. It documents Windows Autopilot support for blocking catalog apps in the Enrollment Status Page and Device Preparation Page. Most updates are expected within 24 hours, while updates requiring manual testing typically take seven days. The page identifies EAM as7

For Intune administrators

Evaluate the Edge capability for opt-in contractor and partner scenarios, focusing on app protection, download redirection, and leak controls. For EPM standard-user migrations, use the documented audit settings and allow 24 hours for reporting data to appear; the guide says longer observation periods may be useful. For WSL compliance, install the Intune WSL plugin, ensure the management extension can install, and remove existing custom WSL compliance policies before setup. For partner MDM and Enterprise App Catalog deployments, confirm licensing and prerequisites, preserve Microsoft-validated app defaults unless deliberately changing them, and plan around the documented update timelines.

This period briefing was generated by AI from the tracked Microsoft Learn and Message Center changes.

New

Microsoft Edge for Business now supports cross-tenant Intune Mobile Application Management (MAM) policies, enabling data protection on devices managed by different tenants. This opt-in feature enforces app protection, redirects downloads to OneDrive, and activates leak controls, enhancing security for contractors and partners without disrupting users.
